domain_label: Plated-Jewelry Poll Specialist — Paid IG/TikTok Reach, Cost-per-Response & Rankable Preference Signal
purpose: A method for running category/attribute preference polls to the ~18-25 US women audience through PAID Instagram/TikTok ads — choosing targeting, campaign objective and poll creative, computing cost-per-response, converting ad clicks/engagement into a confidence-tagged rankable preference signal, knowing when that signal is too weak to act on, and sequencing polls so the ranked candidate list can feed the assortment (six-SKU) decision — without ever inventing a response rate, a cost, or a 'which type girls like' answer the polls themselves must produce.
assumptions: no live campaign has run yet; every CPM, CTR, cost-per-response, response count and preference share is a [METHOD] to be measured or an honest [UNKNOWN], never a fabricated number

the target audience is stated by the owner as mostly young US women ~18-25; platform age/gender/geo targeting is treated as an imperfect proxy for that cohort, not a census (self-reported age and interest inference are noisy) [FACT-platform targeting is inferred]

this KB inherits the instrument design (single-choice vs MaxDiff, option wording, leading-question avoidance) from kb1_instrument_design and the incentive/self-selection/sample-size/giveaway-legal reasoning from kb2_incentive_sampling_bias; it adds only the PAID delivery, cost, and signal-extraction layer on top

native IG/TikTok interactive poll stickers are organic story/native features, not a paid-ad primitive that scales; a paid poll therefore either drives to an explicit instrument (link/lead form) or uses an engagement event as a proxy response [FACT-platform product boundary]

the poll measures stated/engaged preference under paid, incentivized, algorithmically-delivered conditions — a directional demand signal, not revealed purchase behaviour; external validity against real sell-through is a separate step
the output of this KB is a ranked, confidence-tagged candidate list handed to the S5 assortment specialist; this KB does NOT pick the final six SKUs
exclusions: instrument wording, question-type choice (single-choice vs MaxDiff/ranked), and leading/loaded-question avoidance (kb1_instrument_design owns these; this KB consumes the finished instrument)

the mechanics of self-selection/incentive bias, minimum-signal sample-size derivation, and FTC/platform giveaway-sweepstakes law in the general case (kb2_incentive_sampling_bias owns these; this KB uses their results in the paid context)

the final six-SKU launch selection, ABC/Pareto ranking fusion weighting, and cut/keep/expand test-iterate logic (the S5 assortment specialist owns these; this KB stops at the handed-off ranked candidate list)

category/finish demand sizing from public data, consumer segmentation, and trend/competitor mapping (the S1 market specialist owns these; the poll signal is one input the assortment specialist fuses with them)
creative production craft (photography, editing, copywriting) beyond how creative choice confounds the preference signal and how format constrains the response unit
asserting any actual market preference, category ranking, CPM, or cost-per-response as a measured fact; those are produced by running the campaigns this KB specifies

competency_questions.question: What does a PAID IG/TikTok poll actually measure, what can it not tell you, and what decision must it be scoped to before any spend?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PAID_POLL_PREMISE states the paid poll measures stated/engaged preference among a targeted, incentivized, algorithmically-delivered audience (a directional signal, not revealed purchase), and DECISION_TO_INSTRUMENT_LINK fixes the specific assortment decision and its option granularity before budget is committed

competency_questions.question: How is the ~18-25 US women audience actually targeted on Meta/TikTok, and why is platform targeting a proxy rather than a guarantee? [METHOD]
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AUDIENCE_DEFINITION_18_25 names the age/gender/geo/interest/lookalike/custom-audience levers and the honest proxy caveat, and PLATFORM_TARGETING_MECHANICS explains algorithmic (Advantage+/broad optimization) versus narrow manual delivery and how the algorithm, not the marketer, ultimately selects who sees the poll

competency_questions.question: Which campaign objective/optimization event should a poll use, and how does that choice trade cost-per-response against signal quality?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CAMPAIGN_OBJECTIVE_CHOICE contrasts engagement/traffic/lead-or-conversion objectives, shows engagement is cheap but noisy while an explicit instrument (traffic/lead) costs more per response but yields a cleaner vote, and ties the choice to the decision granularity

competency_questions.question: What creative vehicles can carry a poll under paid, given that native poll stickers are organic-only?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NATIVE_STICKER_LIMITATION states the organic-only poll-sticker boundary as [FACT] and POLL_CREATIVE_FORMATS enumerates the paid-viable vehicles (drive-to-instrument link/lead form, A/B thumb-stop creatives, comment-to-vote, interactive engagement units) with their response-unit and bias trade-offs

competency_questions.question: How is cost-per-response computed and turned into the budget needed for a rankable signal? [METHOD]
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COST_PER_RESPONSE_MODEL defines cost-per-response = spend / responses = CPM / (responses per 1000 impressions) decomposed into CPM x CTR/engagement-rate x completion-rate, and SAMPLE_SIZE_BUDGET multiplies the required response count per option (from kb2) by CPR to give the budget, all with [UNKNOWN] live values

competency_questions.question: How does a free-item incentive change response behaviour under a paid poll, and how is it kept from biasing between options?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INCENTIVE_ON_PAID states the incentive lifts response volume and lowers CPR but skews toward deal-seekers and junk/bot responses, and that the incentive framing must be held identical across every option so it does not tilt the between-option comparison [FACT/METHOD]

competency_questions.question: How are raw clicks/engagement events mapped to a countable 'response', and which events are preference expressions versus noise? [METHOD]
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ENGAGEMENT_TO_RESPONSE_MAP defines which event (a completed instrument answer, an option-specific click, a vote) counts as one response and why an impression, a scroll-past, or an undifferentiated like is not a vote

competency_questions.question: How are ad responses turned into a rankable preference signal that a better-funded option cannot simply win? [METHOD]
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SIGNAL_CONSTRUCTION_RANKING normalizes each option to a response-RATE (responses per impression or per dollar), not a raw count, builds a per-option share with a confidence band, and CONFOUND_CONTROL holds creative/format/placement constant and rotates/randomizes so preference is not confounded by spend or creative appeal

competency_questions.question: What statistical check decides whether two options are actually separable rather than tied within noise?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STAT_CONFIDENCE_TEST specifies a two-proportion test / overlapping confidence-interval check on option shares, a minimum detectable difference tied to sample size, and a multiple-comparison caution when many options compete

competency_questions.question: When is the poll signal too weak to act on, and what is the decision rule then? [FACT]
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WEAK_SIGNAL_THRESHOLD gives concrete weak-signal conditions (overlapping CIs, response n below the kb2 minimum, effect size inside noise, CPR so high the budget cannot reach n) and the rule: do not rank, collect more, or fall back to other signals rather than over-reading noise

competency_questions.question: How do platform-reported metrics and stated-versus-revealed preference limit how far the signal can be trusted? [FACT]
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PLATFORM_METRIC_BIAS names bot/fraud, attribution windows, ATT/iOS gaps and algorithmic delivery skew, and STATED_VS_REVEALED states that a poll preference is stated/engaged intent under hypothetical bias and must be validated against real conversion before a full commit

competency_questions.question: How are polls sequenced and fused so the result actually feeds the six-SKU assortment decision? [METHOD]
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POLL_SEQUENCING funnels budget from a cheap broad category screen to narrower within-winner attribute polls, and SIGNAL_FUSION_HANDOFF combines the paid-poll signal with organic/site/market signals weighted by reliability and hands a ranked, confidence-tagged candidate list to S5, stopping before the final six-pick

competency_questions.question: How is honesty discipline enforced so no CPM, cost-per-response, response rate, or preference ranking is stated as measured when it is not?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONESTY_LEDGER separates the [FACT] platform/product boundaries from the [METHOD] measurement procedures and the [UNKNOWN] live numbers, and flags any single-point CPR or preference share as a placeholder to be filled by a run, never a guess

competency_questions.question: What advertising, giveaway, disclosure and privacy compliance binds a paid poll aimed at a young-women audience?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEGAL_PLATFORM_COMPLIANCE states the Meta/TikTok ad-policy limits, FTC endorsement/sweepstakes disclosure, response-data privacy handling, and the requirement to age-gate the targeting to 18+ so the poll and its incentive do not target minors [FACT]

glossary.definition: A preference poll delivered by a PAID IG/TikTok ad campaign to a targeted audience, as opposed to a free native story-poll sticker shown to existing followers; because native poll stickers are organic-only, a paid poll drives to an explicit instrument (link/lead form) or uses an ad engagement event as a proxy response, and pays a measurable cost per response for reach the organic audience cannot supply.

The measured cost of one usable poll response = campaign spend / usable responses = CPM / (responses per 1000 impressions), decomposable as CPM x engagement-or-click-through-rate x completion-rate; it is the unit price the budget buys the signal at, and is a [METHOD] until a live campaign measures it — never a fabricated number.

The single engagement event that is counted as one preference expression — a completed instrument answer, an option-specific click, or a recorded vote — as distinct from an impression, a scroll-past, or an undifferentiated like/follow that expresses no option choice; the response unit must be defined before CPR or any share can be computed.

Ranking options by responses per impression (or per dollar) rather than by raw response count, so an option that simply received more budget or impressions cannot win on exposure; the normalized share is what carries the preference signal, with a confidence band attached.

[FACT] The platform's optimizer, not the marketer, chooses which subset of the targeted audience actually sees the ad, optimizing for the chosen event; this means the responders are a self-selected, algorithm-curated slice, so the measured 'preference' is conditioned on who the algorithm decided would engage, a systematic bias distinct from random sampling error.

The set of conditions under which the poll result must NOT be turned into a ranking: option confidence intervals overlap, usable response count is below the kb2 minimum-signal n, the between-option difference is inside measurement noise, or cost-per-response is so high the reachable budget cannot buy a decisive n; the rule is collect-more or fall-back, not over-read.

[FACT-behavioural] A poll captures stated/engaged preference under hypothetical, incentivized conditions, which is subject to hypothetical bias and is not the same as revealed preference (actual purchase); a poll winner is a hypothesis to validate against real sell-through, not a proven seller.

The outcome the ad platform is told to optimize for (engagement, traffic/link-clicks, or leads/conversions); it sets both who the algorithm targets and what a 'response' costs — engagement is cheapest but noisiest, an explicit instrument (traffic/lead) costs more per response but yields a cleaner, attributable vote.

[METHOD] Spending in stages — a cheap broad category-level screen (earrings vs necklaces vs rings...) first, then funneling budget into a within-winning-category attribute poll (shape/finish/price) — rather than one large multi-question poll, so budget concentrates on live options and each stage's winner defines the next stage's options.

The deliverable this KB produces: a confidence-tagged, reliability-weighted ranked list of candidate categories/attributes handed to the S5 assortment specialist, which fuses it with market and existing-store signals to pick the final six SKUs; this KB explicitly does not make that final pick.

nodes.definition: Establish what a PAID IG/TikTok poll is and honestly bounds. It buys reach the owner's organic follower base cannot supply, delivering a preference instrument to a targeted, incentivized, algorithmically-selected audience and paying a measurable cost per response. What it measures: stated/engaged preference among that slice — a directional demand signal [METHOD to obtain, not a fact to assert]. What it cannot do: it does not measure revealed purchase behaviour, it does not sample the US population (only whoever the platform's optimizer served), and it produces no market number until a campaign actually runs. Every CPM, cost-per-response, response rate and 'which type wins' figure is [UNKNOWN] here and is filled only by running the specified campaigns; nothing about audience preference is asserted as fact in this KB.

nodes.definition: Define the ~18-25 US women audience in platform targeting terms and state the honest caveat. Levers on Meta (IG) and TikTok Ads Manager: age 18-25, gender = women, geo = US (or specific states/DMAs), interest/behaviour targeting (fashion, jewelry, specific style affinities), lookalike/similar audiences seeded from the owner's existing customer/pixel list, and custom audiences (site visitors, engagers) [METHOD-targeting levers]. The binding caveat: platform age and interest data are INFERRED and self-reported, not verified — 'women 18-25 interested in jewelry' is a proxy for the cohort, not a census, and the delivered audience is further narrowed by the optimizer (see PLATFORM_TARGETING_MECHANICS). Do not treat the targeting spec as proof of who actually responded [FACT-inferred targeting].

nodes.definition: Explain how the audience is actually served, because the algorithm, not the targeting spec, decides who sees the poll. Meta's Advantage+ audience and TikTok's broad/automatic targeting increasingly favour a broad seed plus optimizer discretion over narrow manual audiences; the optimizer serves impressions to whoever it predicts will produce the chosen event most cheaply [FACT-algorithmic delivery]. Consequence for a poll: the responders are an optimizer-curated, self-selected slice, so the measured preference is conditioned on who the algorithm decided would engage — a systematic skew distinct from random sampling error (formalized in PLATFORM_METRIC_BIAS). Practical rule: for a preference measurement, avoid letting an engagement optimizer over-concentrate delivery on a lookalike of past engagers, which would bias the poll toward existing-fan taste rather than the target cohort [METHOD-delivery-aware design].

nodes.definition: Choose the campaign objective/optimization event, because it sets both delivery and cost-per-response. Options: (a) engagement/awareness — cheapest impressions and interactions but the noisiest 'response' (a like or view is not an option choice); (b) traffic/link-clicks — drives to an explicit off-platform instrument, moderate cost, an attributable click as the response; (c) leads/conversions — an in-form or on-site completed answer, highest cost per response but the cleanest, most decision-usable vote. Rule: match the objective to the response unit the decision needs — a category screen can tolerate a cheap engagement proxy, but an attribute poll that must be rankable with confidence should optimize for the explicit instrument despite higher CPR [METHOD-objective-to-response-unit match].

pros.example: a cheap engagement objective for the broad category screen, a conversion objective for the tie-breaking attribute poll, spends each dollar at the right precision

cons.claim: The cleanest objective (conversions) costs the most per response and can price a small budget out of a decisive n
cons.example: optimizing for completed lead-form answers may make the required n unaffordable for a fine attribute poll

failure_modes: optimizing for cheap engagement when the decision needs an attributable vote

nodes.definition: State the product boundary that shapes every paid-poll creative decision: IG and TikTok interactive poll/quiz stickers are ORGANIC story/native-post features, not a paid-ad primitive that can be boosted to a cold targeted audience at scale [FACT-platform product boundary as of authoring; verify current ad-product docs before a run]. You cannot simply run a paid ad that IS a tappable story poll sticker to strangers the way you can post one to your own followers. Therefore a paid poll must either (a) drive the targeted audience to an explicit instrument (a linked landing page / lead form / off-platform survey), or (b) use an ad engagement event (option-specific click, comment-to-vote, A/B creative choice) as a proxy response. This constraint is why cost-per-response is higher for a paid poll than a free organic sticker and why the response unit must be defined explicitly.

pros.example: knowing this early routes the design to a link/lead-form instrument instead of a dead-end sticker-boost idea

cons.claim: The alternatives (drive-to-instrument, engagement proxy) each add friction or noise the free sticker avoids

nodes.definition: Enumerate the creative vehicles a paid poll can actually use and their response-unit and bias trade-offs, given the organic-only sticker limit. (1) Drive-to-instrument: ad -> linked landing page / lead form / off-platform survey; response = a completed answer; cleanest and most rankable, but a click-then-complete funnel that raises CPR and drops completion. (2) A/B thumb-stop creatives: run one ad variant per option (earring ad vs necklace ad) to the SAME audience and read comparative engagement rate as the vote; response = option-specific engagement; cheap and native but confounds category preference with creative appeal (see CONFOUND_CONTROL). (3) Comment-to-vote / poll-in-caption: response = a categorized comment; cheap, high-noise, hard to attribute. (4) Interactive/engagement ad units where available. Choose the vehicle by the objective and the required response cleanliness [METHOD-vehicle selection].

nodes.definition: Handle the owner's 'get something free to attract them to select one' incentive in the paid context, building on kb2_incentive_sampling_bias. Effect: an incentive (giveaway entry, discount code) lifts response volume and lowers cost-per-response, but it skews the responder pool toward deal-seekers and sweepstakes-hunters and invites junk/bot entries — inflating volume while degrading the representativeness of the preference [FACT/METHOD; magnitude [UNKNOWN] until measured]. Critical controls: (1) hold the incentive framing IDENTICAL across every option so it lifts all options equally and does not tilt the between-option comparison; (2) treat incentivized responses as a separate stratum to compare against any organic responses; (3) de-duplicate and bot-filter entries. The incentive buys reach and response rate at the cost of pool quality, and its giveaway mechanics are legally constrained (see LEGAL_PLATFORM_COMPLIANCE).

nodes.definition: Define cost-per-response (CPR) and its decomposition so budget can be planned and diagnosed. CPR = campaign spend / usable responses = CPM / (usable responses per 1000 impressions), and usable-responses-per-1000-impressions = 1000 x CTR-or-engagement-rate x completion-rate x usable-fraction (after bot/junk filtering). This makes CPR diagnosable: a high CPR is a high-CPM (audience-cost) problem, a low-CTR (creative/hook) problem, a low-completion (funnel-friction) problem, or a high-junk (incentive/bot) problem — each with a different fix. All inputs (CPM, CTR, completion) are [UNKNOWN] until a live run; this KB supplies the FORMULA and the diagnostic decomposition, never fabricated cost figures [METHOD-CPR model].

included: CPR = spend/usable-responses = CPM/(usable responses per 1000 impressions)
the CPM x CTR x completion x usable-fraction decomposition
diagnosing a high CPR to its driver

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a measured CPM/CTR/completion or funnel change updates the CPR model

pros.claim: A decomposed CPR formula turns a single blended cost into a diagnosable chain so the right lever is pulled
pros.example: a high CPR traced to low completion points to funnel friction, not to raising the bid

cons.claim: The formula's inputs are all [UNKNOWN] pre-run, so CPR is a planning structure not a quotable number until a campaign measures it

nodes.definition: Convert the minimum-signal sample size into a budget and a feasibility check. Budget = (required usable responses per option x number of options) x CPR, where the required-n per option comes from kb2_incentive_sampling_bias's minimum-signal / precision reasoning (enough to separate options at the target confidence and minimum detectable difference). Two directions of use: (a) forward — given a budget, back out the achievable n per option and therefore the finest difference the poll can detect; (b) inverse — given a decision that needs to separate close options, compute the n and hence the budget required, and flag if that budget is infeasible. If the required budget to reach a decisive n exceeds what the owner will spend, the honest output is that the poll cannot answer that question at that granularity [METHOD-budget sizing].

included: budget = required-n x options x CPR
forward (budget->detectable difference) and inverse (difference->budget) use
flagging an infeasible budget as a poll that cannot answer the question

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a measured CPR, option count, or budget ceiling changes the sizing

pros.claim: Tying budget to required-n x CPR makes affordability and detectable-difference explicit before spending
pros.example: showing that separating two near-tied finishes needs an n the budget cannot buy stops a doomed spend

nodes.definition: Define which platform engagement events count as one preference response and which are noise, because the response unit determines everything downstream. A response is an event that expresses an OPTION CHOICE: a completed instrument answer, an option-specific link click (earring-ad click vs necklace-ad click), a categorized vote/comment. NOT responses: an impression, a 3-second view, a scroll-past, an undifferentiated like/follow/share that names no option, or a profile visit. State the mapping explicitly per creative vehicle before counting, and record the usable-fraction after removing bots/junk/duplicates. This node is the hinge between raw platform metrics and any preference share: miscounting an ambiguous like as a vote corrupts every rate and rank downstream [METHOD-response-unit definition].

included: which events are option-expressing responses vs noise
per-vehicle response-unit definition before counting
the usable-fraction after bot/junk/dup removal

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an available-event, reported-metric, or usable-fraction change occurs

pros.claim: Defining the response unit before counting keeps ambiguous engagement from being laundered into votes
pros.example: counting only option-specific clicks, not generic likes, keeps the earrings-vs-necklaces share honest

cons.claim: A strict response definition discards a lot of soft engagement, shrinking usable n and requiring more spend
cons.example: dropping generic likes as non-votes can cut counted responses sharply and raise effective CPR

failure_modes: counting undifferentiated likes/views as option votes
leaving the response unit undefined so different vehicles' counts are silently mixed
acceptance_tests: the option-expressing response events are distinguished from non-response noise per vehicle, with the usable-fraction defined after bot/junk/duplicate removal
revisit_triggers: a creative vehicle changes the available engagement events
a platform changes what metrics it reports
the bot/junk detection method changes the usable-fraction

nodes.definition: Enumerate the ways platform-reported metrics mislead a preference read, so the signal is discounted appropriately. (1) Bot/click-fraud and fake engagement inflate counts, especially under an incentive. (2) Attribution windows and de-duplication choices change what 'a response' totals. (3) ATT/iOS and privacy limits create measurement gaps and modelled (estimated) conversions the platform reports as if observed. (4) Algorithmic delivery skew (from PLATFORM_TARGETING_MECHANICS) means responders are an optimizer-curated slice, so the share reflects who the algorithm served, not the target cohort at large. These are SYSTEMATIC biases, not random error a bigger n fixes — they bias direction, so a large but skewed sample can be confidently wrong [FACT-platform measurement limits]. Every reported figure is treated as an upper bound on signal quality, and the usable-fraction and delivery pattern are logged with each result.

included: bot/fraud, attribution windows, ATT/iOS gaps, algorithmic delivery skew
these being systematic (not random) biases a bigger n does not fix
logging usable-fraction and delivery pattern per result

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a platform measurement, privacy, or fraud-pattern change occurs

pros.claim: Cataloguing the systematic biases stops a large sample from being mistaken for an unbiased one
pros.example: flagging algorithmic delivery skew explains why a confident 70/30 share may still not represent the cohort

cons.claim: Discounting every metric for bias can make any result feel untrustworthy and stall a decision
cons.example: over-weighting fraud fears could reject a genuinely clean, decisive signal

failure_modes: treating reported engagement as clean, unbiased data
assuming a larger sample cures a systematic delivery or fraud bias
acceptance_tests: bot/fraud, attribution, ATT/iOS gaps and algorithmic delivery skew are named as systematic biases that a larger n does not fix, with reported metrics treated as an upper bound and delivery/usable-fraction logged
revisit_triggers: a platform changes attribution or privacy handling

nodes.definition: Control the confounds that would make the poll measure something other than category/attribute preference. Chief confound: creative quality — in an A/B creative vote a prettier or better-lit earring image can beat a necklace on CREATIVE appeal, not category preference. Others: placement (feed vs story vs Reels), time-of-day/day-of-week, audience overlap between ad sets, and budget imbalance across options. Controls: hold creative style, model, background, copy and format constant across options (vary only the product); randomize/rotate placement and schedule; run options in the same audience and time window; equalize or normalize budget per option; and where possible use a within-instrument choice (all options on one screen) rather than separate ads so the same respondent chooses [METHOD-experimental control]. Uncontrolled confounds are the most common reason a confident poll result is simply wrong.

included: creative-quality, placement, timing, overlap and budget confounds
controls: hold creative constant, randomize placement/schedule, same audience/window, normalize budget, within-instrument choice
confounds as the top cause of a confidently wrong result

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a creative, placement, budget-balance, or format change alters the confound set

pros.claim: Holding everything but the product constant makes the measured difference attributable to category/attribute preference, not creative or delivery
pros.example: identical framing with only the pictured product changed isolates earring-vs-necklace preference from photo quality

cons.claim: Rigorous control (matched creative, single-screen choice) constrains creative freedom and can reduce the native scroll-stopping performance that drives cheap reach
cons.example: a deliberately plain matched creative may earn less engagement than an optimized one, raising CPR

failure_modes: running an A/B category vote with unmatched creative quality
letting budget, placement or timing differ across options and attributing the gap to preference
acceptance_tests: the creative/placement/timing/overlap/budget confounds are named with controls (hold creative constant, randomize/rotate, same audience-window, normalize budget, prefer within-instrument choice)
revisit_triggers: a new creative variant or placement is introduced
an imbalance in budget/delivery across options is detected

nodes.definition: Turn usable responses into a rankable preference signal that spend cannot buy. Steps: (1) for each option compute a response RATE — usable responses per impression (or per dollar) — NOT a raw count, so an option that merely received more impressions/budget cannot win on exposure. (2) Compute each option's share of normalized preference with a confidence interval sized by its usable n. (3) Rank options by the normalized share, attaching the confidence band and the usable n to every rank. (4) Carry the incentive stratum, delivery pattern and usable-fraction alongside so the rank is auditable. The output is a ranked list of options each tagged with its normalized share, CI and n — the core deliverable — and it is only as trustworthy as the confounds controlled and the separability test that follows [METHOD-signal construction].

included: response-RATE normalization per impression/dollar
per-option normalized share with a CI and usable n
a ranked, auditable option list as the core deliverable

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new responses, a confound change, or an option-set change updates the ranking

pros.claim: Ranking by normalized response rate with a CI stops a better-funded option from winning on exposure and makes each rank auditable
pros.example: necklaces at 8% response-rate beating earrings at 6%, each with its CI and n, is a defensible rank; raw vote counts would just reflect budget

cons.claim: Normalization and CIs make the output a banded ranking, not a crisp winner, which can frustrate a decision wanting one answer
cons.example: two options whose CIs overlap produce a tie the ranking must honestly report

failure_modes: ranking by raw response count so the best-funded option wins
reporting a rank without its confidence interval and usable n
acceptance_tests: options are ranked by normalized response rate (per impression/dollar) with a confidence interval and usable n attached to each, and the incentive/delivery/usable-fraction carried for audit
revisit_triggers: more responses arrive and tighten the CIs
a confound-control or usable-fraction change alters the rates
an option is added or removed

nodes.definition: Decide whether two options are actually separable rather than tied within noise. Method: a two-proportion z-test (or equivalent) on the normalized option shares, or the simpler check of whether their confidence intervals overlap; the minimum detectable difference is set by the usable n per option (from SAMPLE_SIZE_BUDGET). When many options compete, apply a multiple-comparison caution (e.g. Bonferroni-style adjustment) so one of several options does not appear to win by chance. Output per option pair: separable (act on the rank) or not-separable (a tie to break with more data or another signal). This is the gate that converts a raw ranking into an actionable-or-not verdict and directly feeds the weak-signal rule [FACT/METHOD-hypothesis testing].

included: two-proportion test / overlapping-CI check on option shares
minimum detectable difference from usable n
multiple-comparison adjustment across many options

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a usable-n, option-count, or required-confidence change updates the test

pros.claim: A formal separability test prevents ranking two statistically tied options as if one clearly won
pros.example: a 52/48 split whose CIs overlap is correctly reported as not separable rather than a necklace win

cons.claim: Requiring statistical separability raises the n (and budget) needed to call close options, sometimes beyond reach
cons.example: separating two near-equal shapes at 95% confidence may need an n the budget cannot buy

failure_modes: declaring a winner between options whose CIs overlap
running many pairwise comparisons without a multiple-comparison correction
acceptance_tests: a two-proportion / overlapping-CI separability test is specified with a minimum detectable difference tied to usable n and a multiple-comparison caution for many options
revisit_triggers: usable n changes the minimum detectable difference
the number of competing options changes
a closer decision demands a higher confidence level

nodes.definition: State when the poll signal is too weak to act on and what to do instead — the owner's explicit '[FACT] when the signal is too weak' question. Weak-signal conditions (any one triggers): (1) the top options' confidence intervals overlap after the separability test; (2) usable response n is below the kb2 minimum-signal threshold; (3) the between-option difference is inside the measurement-bias band (smaller than the systematic bias in PLATFORM_METRIC_BIAS); (4) cost-per-response is so high the reachable budget cannot buy a decisive n. Decision rule when weak: do NOT force a ranking — either collect more data (extend spend/time to reach n), simplify the question (fewer, more distinct options), or fall back to other demand signals (market read, existing-store sell-through) and label the poll inconclusive. Forcing a decision on a weak signal is worse than admitting the poll did not resolve it [FACT-honest inference discipline].

included: the four weak-signal trigger conditions
the collect-more / simplify / fall-back decision rule
labelling the poll inconclusive rather than forcing a rank

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a data, bias-band, or decision-tolerance change flips the weak-signal verdict

pros.claim: An explicit weak-signal rule prevents a noisy poll from driving a false-confident assortment decision
pros.example: overlapping CIs on the top two categories trigger 'inconclusive, collect more' instead of a coin-flip pick

cons.claim: A strict threshold can leave a decision unresolved and force reliance on slower or costlier signals
cons.example: declaring the poll inconclusive may push the choice back onto limited existing-store data

failure_modes: forcing a ranking when CIs overlap or n is below threshold
acting on a between-option gap smaller than the systematic measurement bias
acceptance_tests: the four weak-signal conditions (overlapping CIs, n below minimum, difference inside the bias band, budget cannot reach n) and the collect-more/simplify/fall-back rule are stated, with the poll labelled inconclusive rather than forced
revisit_triggers: more data changes whether a condition is met
the measurement-bias band is re-estimated
the decision's tolerance for inconclusive changes

nodes.definition: State the external-validity ceiling on any poll winner. A poll captures STATED/engaged preference under hypothetical, incentivized, low-commitment conditions (tapping an option costs nothing), which is subject to hypothetical bias and social/aspirational answering; it is NOT REVEALED preference (spending money) [FACT-behavioural economics; stated-vs-revealed / hypothetical-bias]. Consequences: a poll winner is a demand HYPOTHESIS, not a proven seller, and the gap between stated and revealed is largest exactly where an incentive is involved. Discipline: treat the ranked poll result as a candidate to VALIDATE against real conversion — a small paid-conversion test, a pre-order, or a low-quantity live SKU — before committing full inventory. This node is why the handoff is a candidate list, not a launch order, and it bounds how far the assortment specialist should lean on the poll alone.

included: stated/engaged vs revealed (purchase) preference and hypothetical bias
a poll winner as a hypothesis to validate against real conversion
why the deliverable is a candidate list not a launch order
excluded: the actual conversion-test design and the six-SKU pick (S5)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a revealed-preference test or incentive-effect re-estimate updates the validity gap

pros.claim: Naming the stated-vs-revealed gap stops a poll winner from being treated as a proven seller and routes it to validation
pros.example: a category that wins the poll gets a small live-SKU conversion test before a full inventory commit

cons.claim: Insisting on revealed-preference validation adds time and cost before the poll can drive a launch
cons.example: a conversion test delays the assortment decision the poll was meant to speed up

failure_modes: treating a stated-preference poll winner as a proven purchase driver
committing full inventory to a poll winner without any revealed-preference check
acceptance_tests: the poll is stated to measure stated/engaged (not revealed) preference under hypothetical bias, with the winner treated as a hypothesis to validate against real conversion before a full commit
revisit_triggers: a conversion test returns revealed-preference data
the incentive's role in inflating stated preference is re-estimated
the owner's risk tolerance for unvalidated commits changes

nodes.definition: Sequence polls so budget concentrates on live options instead of one giant multi-question poll. Stage 1: a cheap, broad category screen (earrings vs necklaces vs rings vs bracelets vs anklets) at a low CPR to eliminate clearly weak categories. Stage 2: fund a within-winning-category attribute poll (shape, then finish — e.g. rhodium-plated silver vs gold-plated look — then price band) at a cleaner objective/higher CPR because fewer options need separating. Stage 3: narrow to the finalists that the six-SKU assortment can consume. Each stage's separable winners (from STAT_CONFIDENCE_TEST) define the next stage's options; weak-signal stages (WEAK_SIGNAL_THRESHOLD) either repeat with more budget or hand their tie forward unresolved. This funnels spend to where it changes the decision and avoids paying to separate options already eliminated [METHOD-sequential design].

included: cheap broad category screen then funded within-winner attribute polls
each stage's separable winner defining the next stage's options
weak stages repeating or handing a tie forward
excluded: the fusion with non-poll signals and the final handoff (SIGNAL_FUSION_HANDOFF)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a stage result, required-attribute, or stage-budget change updates the sequence

pros.claim: Sequencing concentrates budget on live options and never pays to separate already-eliminated ones
pros.example: spending Stage-2 budget only within the winning category buys a decisive n where a single mega-poll would have spread thin

cons.claim: Staging adds calendar time and lets a Stage-1 elimination error propagate — a category wrongly screened out never gets a Stage-2 look
cons.example: a category eliminated on a weak Stage-1 read is lost even if it would have won on attributes

failure_modes: running one giant multi-question poll that under-powers every option
eliminating a category on a Stage-1 signal that was itself weak/inconclusive
acceptance_tests: a broad cheap category screen then funded within-winner attribute stages are specified, with each stage's separable winner setting the next options and weak stages repeating or passing a tie forward
revisit_triggers: a stage returns a weak/inconclusive result
the assortment decision's required attributes change
budget for a later stage changes

nodes.definition: Carry the binding compliance flags for a paid poll aimed at young women with an incentive. (1) Ad-platform policy: Meta and TikTok advertising policies govern targeting, creative and data use; a policy violation can disable the ad account mid-campaign. (2) Giveaway/sweepstakes law + FTC: an incentive/giveaway is a promotion with official-rules, no-purchase-necessary and disclosure requirements, and any creator/affiliate amplification must disclose the material connection (FTC endorsement guides) [FACT — builds on kb2's giveaway-law node]. (3) Data/privacy: collecting responses (especially via a lead form or off-platform survey) triggers privacy-notice and data-handling obligations. (4) Age: the audience must be age-gated to 18+ so neither the poll nor its incentive targets minors — a hard constraint on the age-targeting lever [FACT]. These are gates to clear before spend, not optional polish.

included: Meta/TikTok ad-policy compliance
giveaway/sweepstakes + FTC endorsement/disclosure
response-data privacy handling and 18+ age-gating

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a platform-policy, giveaway-law, privacy, or age-rule change occurs

pros.claim: Clearing ad-policy, giveaway, privacy and age gates before spend prevents a mid-campaign account shutdown or a legal exposure
pros.example: posting official giveaway rules and age-gating to 18+ keeps the incentive campaign compliant and live

cons.claim: Compliance adds setup work and can constrain the most engaging incentive or targeting
cons.example: official-rules and 18+ gating reduce the reach and simplicity of the incentive hook

failure_modes: running an incentive giveaway without official rules / FTC disclosure
failing to age-gate so the poll or incentive reaches minors
acceptance_tests: Meta/TikTok ad-policy, giveaway/sweepstakes + FTC disclosure, response-data privacy, and 18+ age-gating are stated as gates to clear before spend
revisit_triggers: a platform ad policy or the FTC endorsement/giveaway guidance changes
the incentive mechanic changes
a privacy-law change affects response-data handling

nodes.definition: Compose the deliverable: fuse the paid-poll signal with the other demand signals and hand a ranked, confidence-tagged candidate list to the S5 assortment specialist, then stop. The paid-poll rank (from SIGNAL_CONSTRUCTION_RANKING, gated by STAT_CONFIDENCE_TEST and WEAK_SIGNAL_THRESHOLD, bounded by STATED_VS_REVEALED) is ONE input; it is combined with the S1 market read and the owner's existing-store sell-through, each WEIGHTED BY RELIABILITY (revealed sell-through > validated poll > stated poll > inferred market estimate). The handoff states, per candidate: its normalized poll share and CI, its separability verdict, its stated-vs-revealed validation status, and its fused rank — and explicitly does NOT pick the final six SKUs (that is S5). Where the poll was inconclusive, the handoff says so and defers to the other signals rather than inventing a poll winner [METHOD-reliability-weighted fusion].

included: fusing the poll rank with market and existing-store signals weighted by reliability
a per-candidate handoff (share+CI, separability, validation status, fused rank)
stopping before the six-SKU pick and deferring on inconclusive polls
excluded: the final six-SKU selection and ABC/Pareto logic (S5)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new signal, a weighting revision, or an S5 handoff-format change occurs

pros.claim: A reliability-weighted fusion keeps a stated-preference poll from over-driving the assortment while still using its signal
pros.example: weighting validated sell-through above a stated poll stops a hypothetical poll winner from dominating the six-pick

cons.claim: Reliability weights are themselves judgement calls, and a poorly chosen weight can under- or over-use the poll
cons.example: over-weighting a thin poll over sparse store data could still mislead the fused rank

failure_modes: letting the poll rank override more reliable revealed sell-through
inventing a poll winner for a stage the weak-signal rule marked inconclusive
drifting into making the six-SKU pick this KB does not own
acceptance_tests: the poll rank is fused with market and existing-store signals weighted by reliability into a per-candidate handoff (share+CI, separability, validation status, fused rank) that stops before the six-SKU pick and defers on inconclusive polls
revisit_triggers: a more reliable signal (validated sell-through) arrives

nodes.definition: Enforce the honesty discipline across the paid-poll work so no number is stated as measured when it is not. Solid [FACT] (load-bearing, cited/verifiable): native poll stickers are organic-only; algorithmic delivery selects responders; platform metrics carry bot/attribution/ATT bias; stated preference is not revealed preference; giveaway/FTC/age-gating rules bind. [METHOD] (procedures, not numbers): the targeting spec, the CPR decomposition, the sample-size-to-budget conversion, the response-unit mapping, the normalized-rate ranking, the separability test, the weak-signal rule, the sequencing and the reliability-weighted fusion. [UNKNOWN] until a run: every CPM, CTR, completion rate, cost-per-response, response count, and preference share — and, above all, the answer to 'which type do 18-25 women prefer', which the polls PRODUCE and this KB never guesses. Any single-point CPR or share is a placeholder to be filled by a measured run, never a fabricated figure.

included: the [FACT] platform/behavioural anchors
the [METHOD] procedures that carry no invented numbers
the [UNKNOWN] live metrics and the 'which type they prefer' answer the polls produce
excluded: the substantive method content (the other nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an [UNKNOWN] is measured or a [FACT] anchor changes

pros.claim: A single ledger separating [FACT] anchors from [METHOD] procedures and [UNKNOWN] live numbers keeps the KB trustworthy and un-fabricated
pros.example: tagging CPR a [METHOD] with [UNKNOWN] inputs tells a reader no cost figure here is measured

cons.claim: Heavy tagging can read as evasive to a stakeholder who wants a concrete cost or a definitive preference answer now
cons.example: an owner wanting 'CPR = $X' must accept a formula plus an [UNKNOWN] until a pilot runs

failure_modes: stating a CPM/CPR/preference share as measured when it is a placeholder
letting 'which type they prefer' be answered by guess rather than by a run
acceptance_tests: the [FACT] platform/behavioural anchors, the [METHOD] procedures, and the [UNKNOWN] live metrics (CPM/CTR/CPR/shares and the preference answer) are separated, with any single-point figure flagged a placeholder to be filled by a run
revisit_triggers: a live run fills an [UNKNOWN] with a measured number

conflict_axes.name: incentive_response_lift_vs_pool_bias
conflict_axes.description: A free-item incentive lifts response volume and lowers CPR (helping reach a decisive n) but skews the responder pool toward deal-seekers and bots, degrading the representativeness of the preference it measures.
poles: use the incentive to maximize response volume
minimize the incentive to protect pool quality
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold incentive framing identical across options, stratify incentivized vs organic responses, and trust the organic stratum for direction while using the incentive lift as volume

conflict_axes.name: broad_algorithmic_vs_narrow_manual_targeting
conflict_axes.description: Broad algorithmic (Advantage+/auto) delivery is cheaper and higher-volume but drifts off the 18-25 women cohort, while narrow manual targeting holds the cohort at higher CPM and lower volume.
poles: let the optimizer deliver broadly for cheap volume
constrain manually to hold the target cohort
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: constrain enough to keep the cohort and monitor delivered demographics; accept higher CPM over a cheap broad delivery that biases the responder pool

conflict_axes.name: cheap_engagement_vs_strong_signal
conflict_axes.description: A cheap engagement objective/vehicle minimizes cost-per-response but yields a noisy proxy vote, while an explicit-instrument conversion objective yields a clean rankable vote at a much higher CPR.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: match objective to stage — cheap engagement for the broad screen, clean conversion for the decisive attribute poll — letting required signal quality drive the choice

conflict_axes.name: native_engagement_proxy_vs_explicit_instrument
conflict_axes.description: An engagement-proxy response (like/click) is cheap and native but ambiguous, while an explicit-instrument answer is unambiguous but adds a click-then-complete funnel that raises CPR and lowers volume.
poles: read cheap native engagement as the vote
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the engagement proxy only for coarse screens and require the explicit instrument wherever an option choice must be unambiguous and rankable with confidence

conflict_axes.name: creative_appeal_vs_category_preference
conflict_axes.description: In an A/B creative vote, a better-looking image can win on creative appeal rather than on the category/attribute the poll intends to measure, confounding the preference.
poles: let native optimized creative maximize engagement
hold creative matched to isolate category preference
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold creative style/model/background/copy constant and vary only the product, or use a within-instrument single-screen choice, so the measured difference is category preference not photo quality

conflict_axes.name: speed_cheap_poll_vs_statistical_separability
conflict_axes.description: A fast cheap poll gives a quick ranking but may not buy the n needed to statistically separate close options, so its winner can be a tie dressed as a decision.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: report a rank only when the separability test passes; otherwise label it inconclusive and either collect more or fall back to other signals rather than force a decision

conflict_axes.name: one_big_poll_vs_sequenced_funnel
conflict_axes.description: A single large multi-question poll answers everything at once but under-powers every option, while a sequenced screen-then-narrow funnel concentrates budget but adds calendar time and can propagate an early elimination error.
poles: sequence cheap screen then funded narrow polls
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: sequence, but never eliminate a category on a Stage-1 signal that itself failed the weak-signal test; repeat a weak screen before narrowing

conflict_axes.name: platform_reported_metric_vs_true_preference
conflict_axes.description: Platform-reported engagement is convenient and large but carries bot/attribution/ATT and algorithmic-delivery bias, so a big reported number can be confidently unrepresentative of true preference.
poles: discount every metric for systematic bias
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat reported metrics as an upper bound, log usable-fraction and delivery pattern, and never let a between-option gap smaller than the bias band count as signal

conflict_axes.name: stated_poll_winner_vs_revealed_purchase
conflict_axes.description: The poll's stated-preference winner is fast and cheap to obtain but subject to hypothetical bias, while a revealed-purchase test is costlier and slower yet far more predictive of what actually sells.
poles: act on the stated-preference poll winner
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the poll to prioritize hypotheses but validate the winner with a small revealed-preference (live-SKU/pre-order) test before a full inventory commit, and weight revealed above stated in fusion

edge_cases.description: The top two options' confidence intervals overlap yet the poll is reported as if one clearly won
edge_cases.trigger: a near-tie (e.g. 52/48) is ranked without the separability test
edge_cases.mitigation: run the two-proportion/overlapping-CI test and, if not separable, label it a tie to break with more data or another signal

edge_cases.description: An incentive giveaway floods one option with deal-seeker and bot responses, inflating its share
edge_cases.trigger: a free-item hook attached to a poll without stratification or bot-filtering
edge_cases.mitigation: hold incentive framing identical across options, de-duplicate and bot-filter, and compare the organic stratum against the incentivized one

edge_cases.description: An A/B creative vote is won by the better-looking product image on creative appeal, not category preference
edge_cases.trigger: unmatched creative quality across the option variants
edge_cases.mitigation: hold creative style/model/background/copy constant and vary only the product, or use a single-screen within-instrument choice

edge_cases.description: The optimizer concentrates delivery on a lookalike of past engagers, biasing the poll toward existing-fan taste
edge_cases.trigger: an engagement objective on a broad audience over-fitting delivery to prior engagers
edge_cases.mitigation: use a broader reach objective for the screen, monitor delivered demographics, and constrain the audience to the target cohort

edge_cases.description: Cost-per-response is so high that the reachable budget cannot buy a decisive n for the question asked
edge_cases.trigger: a measured CPR far above plan on a fine attribute poll
edge_cases.mitigation: diagnose the CPR driver and lower it, coarsen the question to fewer options, or declare the poll unable to answer at that granularity

edge_cases.description: A plan assumes a native poll sticker can be paid-boosted to a cold audience at scale
edge_cases.trigger: a paid-poll design built on the organic-only interactive sticker
edge_cases.mitigation: route the paid poll to an explicit instrument or an engagement-proxy vehicle and verify current ad-product docs before spend

edge_cases.description: Broad optimization drifts delivery outside the 18-25 women cohort while the targeting label still reads 18-25
edge_cases.trigger: Advantage+/auto targeting expanding the audience for cheaper delivery
edge_cases.mitigation: constrain the audience, disable aggressive audience expansion for the measurement, and check delivered-age/gender breakdowns

edge_cases.description: One of many competing options appears to win purely by multiple-comparison chance
edge_cases.trigger: ranking 6+ options without a multiple-comparison adjustment
edge_cases.mitigation: apply a Bonferroni-style adjustment or require a larger margin as the option count grows

edge_cases.description: A poll winner is committed to full inventory but fails a real-conversion test
edge_cases.trigger: treating a stated-preference winner as a proven seller without validation
edge_cases.mitigation: validate the winner with a small paid-conversion / pre-order / low-quantity live-SKU test before a full commit

edge_cases.description: The poll rank overrides more reliable existing-store sell-through in the handoff
edge_cases.trigger: weighting a thin stated poll above revealed sell-through in fusion
edge_cases.mitigation: weight revealed sell-through above stated poll preference and use the poll to prioritize, not to override, revealed data

edge_cases.description: An incentive giveaway runs without official rules, FTC disclosure, or 18+ age-gating
edge_cases.trigger: launching the incentive campaign before clearing the compliance gates
edge_cases.mitigation: post official giveaway rules, add required disclosures, age-gate to 18+, and confirm platform ad-policy compliance before spend

workflow.action: Scope the poll to the assortment decision
workflow.description: Fix the S5 six-SKU decision and set category-then-attribute option granularity before any spend
workflow.gate: the poll options are actionable for the six-SKU decision with a defined stage-win meaning

workflow.action: Define the audience and its delivery
workflow.description: Set the 18-25 US women targeting levers and note the inferred-proxy caveat and optimizer delivery behaviour
workflow.gate: the targeting levers and the proxy/algorithmic-delivery caveat are stated

workflow.description: Pick engagement/traffic/conversion by the response unit the stage needs, trading CPR against signal quality
workflow.gate: the objective is matched to the required response unit with its CPR/quality trade stated

workflow.description: Given the organic-only sticker limit, choose drive-to-instrument, A/B, comment-to-vote or interactive with its response unit and bias
workflow.gate: the vehicle, its response unit and its bias trade-off are stated

workflow.action: Design the incentive and clear compliance
workflow.description: Attach the incentive with identical framing across options and clear ad-policy, giveaway/FTC, privacy and 18+ gates
workflow.gate: identical incentive framing plus ad-policy, giveaway, privacy and 18+ gating are cleared

workflow.action: Model CPR and size the budget
workflow.description: Decompose CPR and multiply required-n x options x CPR; flag if a decisive n is unaffordable
workflow.gate: the CPR decomposition and required-n x CPR budget are stated with a feasibility verdict

workflow.description: Fix which engagement events count as an option-expressing response and the usable-fraction after bot/junk removal
workflow.gate: the option-expressing responses vs noise and the usable-fraction are defined per vehicle

workflow.action: Control confounds and log delivery bias
workflow.description: Hold creative constant, randomize placement/schedule, normalize budget, and log delivery pattern and metric biases
workflow.gate: the confound controls and logged delivery/usable-fraction are in place

workflow.description: Normalize to response rate per impression/dollar and rank options with a CI and usable n each
workflow.gate: options are ranked by normalized rate with CI and usable n attached

workflow.action: Test separability and the weak-signal rule
workflow.description: Run the separability test and apply the weak-signal conditions; label inconclusive rather than force a rank
workflow.gate: each rank is either separable-and-actionable or labelled inconclusive with the collect-more/fall-back rule

workflow.description: Funnel budget from the broad category screen into a within-winner attribute poll, or repeat a weak stage
workflow.gate: each separable winner sets the next stage's options and weak stages repeat or pass a tie forward

workflow.action: Fuse and hand off the ranked candidates
workflow.description: Weight the poll signal against market and existing-store signals by reliability and hand a confidence-tagged candidate list to S5, stopping before the six-pick
workflow.gate: the per-candidate handoff (share+CI, separability, validation status, fused rank) stops before the six-SKU pick and defers on inconclusive polls

priority_rationale: The premise, decision link, audience, delivery mechanics, objective and native-sticker limit come first because they fix what the poll measures, for whom, at what response unit, and within what platform product boundary — every cost and signal number depends on them; the creative vehicle, incentive, CPR model, budget sizing, response mapping and metric-bias catalogue next, because they are the instrumentation and cost layer that turns reach into countable responses; the confound control, normalized ranking, separability test, weak-signal rule and stated-vs-revealed bound then convert responses into a trustworthy-or-inconclusive signal; and the sequencing, compliance, fusion handoff and honesty ledger come last because they compose the staged spend, the legal gates, the reliability-weighted ranked candidate list handed to S5, and the discipline that no live number is ever fabricated.

dominance_rules.rule: The weak-signal rule dominates any pressure to produce a ranked winner
dominance_rules.rationale: forcing a decision on overlapping CIs or a sub-threshold n is worse than admitting the poll did not resolve it
dominance_rules.trigger: a stakeholder wants a ranked winner but the separability test fails
dominance_rules.action: label the result inconclusive and collect more, simplify the question, or fall back to other signals

dominance_rules.rule: Normalized response rate dominates raw response count in ranking
dominance_rules.rationale: raw counts reward whichever option got more impressions or budget, not preference
dominance_rules.trigger: a ranking is drawn from raw vote counts
dominance_rules.action: re-rank by responses per impression/dollar with a CI and usable n per option

dominance_rules.rule: Revealed sell-through dominates stated poll preference in fusion
dominance_rules.rationale: stated preference is subject to hypothetical bias while revealed purchase actually predicts sales
dominance_rules.trigger: a fused rank is about to weight a stated poll above revealed sell-through
dominance_rules.action: weight revealed above stated and require a revealed-preference validation before a full commit

dominance_rules.rule: Signal quality dominates lowest CPR in objective/vehicle choice for a decisive poll
dominance_rules.rationale: a cheap noisy response cannot separate close options no matter how many are bought
dominance_rules.trigger: a decisive attribute poll is set to the cheapest engagement objective
dominance_rules.action: use the explicit-instrument conversion objective for the decisive stage even at higher CPR

dominance_rules.rule: Systematic bias dominates a small between-option gap
dominance_rules.rationale: a difference smaller than the bot/attribution/delivery bias band is noise a larger n does not fix
dominance_rules.trigger: an option leads by less than the estimated measurement-bias band
dominance_rules.action: treat the gap as inconclusive and do not act on it as signal

dominance_rules.rule: Matched creative dominates optimized creative in an A/B category vote
dominance_rules.rationale: unmatched creative measures photo appeal, not category preference
dominance_rules.trigger: an A/B vote uses differently-optimized images per option
dominance_rules.action: hold creative constant and vary only the product, or use a within-instrument single-screen choice

dominance_rules.rationale: a policy/giveaway/age violation can disable the account or create legal exposure mid-run
dominance_rules.trigger: an incentive campaign is ready to launch without cleared gates
dominance_rules.action: clear ad-policy, giveaway/FTC disclosure, privacy and 18+ gating before any spend

dominance_rules.rule: The candidate handoff never becomes the six-SKU pick
dominance_rules.rationale: the assortment selection is S5's owned decision that fuses more than the poll
dominance_rules.trigger: the poll work starts choosing the final six items
dominance_rules.action: stop at the ranked, confidence-tagged candidate list and hand off to S5

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the assortment decision and option granularity before buying any reach
anti_rework_rules.prevents: spending a full ad budget on a question too vague or mis-grained for the six-SKU decision to consume

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run a small CPR pilot before committing the full poll budget
anti_rework_rules.prevents: sizing a budget on an assumed CPR that is 2-3x off and buying far too few responses to separate options

anti_rework_rules.rule: Define the response unit and usable-fraction before counting any results
anti_rework_rules.prevents: mixing ambiguous likes with option clicks and having to recompute every rate and rank later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Match creative and hold format constant from the first A/B poll
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a creative-quality confound that invalidates the category read and forces the whole poll to be re-run

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach a confidence interval and usable n to every rank as it is produced
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a raw ranking circulating as decisive and later having to be retracted as a statistical tie

anti_rework_rules.rule: Clear giveaway/FTC/privacy/age-gating compliance before launch, not after
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a mid-campaign account shutdown or legal exposure that wastes the spend and the calendar

anti_rework_rules.rule: Never eliminate a category on a Stage-1 screen that itself failed the weak-signal test
anti_rework_rules.prevents: propagating a weak early elimination that permanently drops a category the later stage would have surfaced

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every CPM/CPR/share as [UNKNOWN] until a run measures it, from the first draft
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a fabricated placeholder number hardening into a quoted figure that must later be corrected

iteration_protocol.trigger: a CPR pilot returns measured CPM/CTR/completion
iteration_protocol.action: fill the CPR model and re-size the budget and achievable n per option

iteration_protocol.trigger: a poll stage returns a weak or inconclusive result
iteration_protocol.action: apply the weak-signal rule and either extend spend, simplify the options, or fall back to other signals before narrowing

iteration_protocol.trigger: delivered demographics or delivery pattern drift off the 18-25 women cohort
iteration_protocol.action: re-constrain the audience and disable aggressive expansion, then re-log the delivery bias

iteration_protocol.trigger: an incentivized vs organic stratum disagreement or a bot spike appears
iteration_protocol.action: re-filter, re-stratify, and trust the organic stratum for the preference direction

iteration_protocol.trigger: a stage winner passes separability and is ready to narrow
iteration_protocol.action: define the next stage's options from the winner and fund the within-winner attribute poll

iteration_protocol.trigger: a revealed-preference (live-SKU/pre-order) test returns conversion data
iteration_protocol.action: update the validation status and re-weight the fused rank toward revealed preference

iteration_protocol.trigger: a platform ad policy, interactive-poll product, or FTC/giveaway rule changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-check the native-sticker limit, creative vehicle and compliance gates before the next run
